title: Intervals: Seconds to Fifths
description: Learn to see and hear the distance between two notes: a second, third, fourth and fifth from middle C, each played one note at a time (melodic) and then together (harmonic).

arrangements.label: Beginner
arrangements.notes: Right hand measures intervals upward from C4 (C-D, C-E, C-F, C-G) and the left hand downward from C4 (C-B, C-A, C-G, C-F); each bar is two single notes then the dyad.
teachingPoints: An interval is counted by letter names including both ends: C to E is a third (C-D-E), C to G is a fifth.
Bars 1-4: thumb stays on middle C; the finger number equals the interval number (2nd = finger 2, 3rd = finger 3...).
Bars 5-8: the same intervals downward in the left hand, thumb on middle C, finger number again equals the interval.
Listen: seconds clash, thirds are sweet, fourths and fifths sound open and hollow - try to name them with your eyes closed.
